Closes #714

Pin `requests.Session().trust_env = False` on every `OpenStudioClient` instance to prevent environment-variable-driven proxy interception of the in-cluster REST traffic.

The `requests` library (>=2.32) defaults to honoring `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` / `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` / `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` — a compromised or misconfigured host env (or an attacker who controls env injection, the #678 USER-shape attack class) could transparently redirect `GET /analyses.json` through an attacker-controlled proxy. The operator runs with `capabilities.drop=["ALL"]` + `readOnlyRootFilesystem=true` so the env injection surface is bounded, but kopf's own process inherits the pod env wholesale — pinning `trust_env=False` keeps the operator's REST traffic on the explicit `self._base` URL with no proxy fallback.

Cluster admins who need a corporate proxy MUST mount the proxy as a sidecar or route through the existing `OPENSTUDIO_TLS_CA_BUNDLE` env var (#242 contract) rather than rely on `HTTPS_PROXY`.

Test coverage:
- New regression test `test_session_trust_env_is_disabled` asserts `_session.trust_env is False` on every new `OpenStudioClient`.
- All 1184 tests pass (was 1183, +1 new).

Scope guard: Do NOT change the `OPENSTUDIO_TLS_CA_BUNDLE` env-var contract (#476); #242 owns that surface. Do NOT add a re-enable opt-in — the default-disables posture is the security boundary.

Extend `openstudio_client._TRANSIENT_EXCEPTIONS` to cover `ChunkedEncodingError`, `ContentDecodingError`, and `SSLError` — the three `requests.exceptions` subclasses that can fire mid-flight during a live deployment but escaped the pre-#716 retry envelope. Test coverage:
- 4 new regression tests: one per transient subclass + a combined exhaustion test that round-trips every subclass through the full 4-attempt envelope.
- All 1187 tests pass (was 1183; +4 new).

Scope guard: Do NOT change the retry COUNT (`max_retries = 3`) or the backoff ceiling; #579 owns the K8s-side retry semantics. Do NOT widen `_TRANSIENT_EXCEPTIONS` to a bare `RequestException` umbrella — the explicit-subclass fence is what keeps `MissingSchema` / `InvalidURL` / `InvalidHeader` (programmer errors) out of the retry envelope.
